author: Parsifal-2045
body: #### PR description This PR was co-developed by the NGT Task 3.1.1 team: @rovere, @mmusich, @JanGerritSchulz, @elenavernazza, @bfonta, @EmanueleCoradin together with inputs from @borzari and @AdrianoDee. In this PR we introduce a new heterogeneous collection of Outer-Tracker stubs, built on device following the existing `VectorHit` formalism. Additionally, the PixelTracking CA is re-envisioned and extended to take full advantage of hits from the Pixel detector and the aforementioned stubs in the OuterTracker. With these developments, we've also included a partial rework of the BrokenLine (heterogeneous) fit to include full material and magnetic field maps in order to improve the quality of the fit. This is the first implementing PR for Iterative Tracking on Accelerators with Cellular Automaton (ITACA), further improvements to the fit and physics reach are expected to follow. Preliminary results for the full chain where shown at the [24/08 TRK POG meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1719987/#1-update-on-extension-of-ca-an). ##### Main developments - New `reco::StubsSoA` / `reco::OTRecHitsSoA` collections (`DataFormats/TrackingRecHitSoA`) with ROOT dictionaries. The CA reads pixel hits and stubs through a single bounds-checked interface (`CAHitsView`), implemented with the same API as the existing SoAMultiView to maintain easy backwards compatibility via type aliasing - The stubs implementation is bundled together with its validation via a new DQM module (+ harvesting) - OT RecHit conversion for pixel seeding (`hltPixelSeedingOTRecHitsSoA`), run-dependent stacked-module geometry (`StackedModuleGeometryESProducer`), and vector-hit-style stub formation kernels (`OTStubProducerVectorHitStyle`) - The cellular automaton is extended to the full tracker, with pixelstub and stubstub doublets, stub-curvature-based triplet criteria, and an optional in-kernel triplet/track DNN (compile-time weight banks, off by default to not change physics, but enabled for ITACA) - The CA kernels and fit orchestration are now split per topology (`Phase1` / `HIonPhase1` / `Phase2` / `Phase2OT` / `Phase2OTStubs`) to reduce single-TU compile times. The fit kernels are now launched from a single fused ladder that replaces per-hit-multiplicity launches - The `BrokenLine` fit is reworked with access to maps describing the material and magnetic field. The fit now walks the Geant4-derived material map cell-by-cell (resolution 0.5 cm, integrated in ). The new (Bz, Br) map describes the bending field and is used to correct the trajectory. All the changes are gated behind a new `useFitCorrections` flags enable only for `Phase2OTStubs` by default to not change physics for any other configuration - The CA can now optionally rely on two in-kernel DNNs (with weights saved as constants in header files) to select High-Purity triplets (`useTripletDNN`) and assign tight quality to tracks (`useTrackDNN`). Again, these flags are only turned on for the new stubs-based CA. Furthermore, for this updated configuration, the final HP selection has replaced the torch DNN with a compact gradient-boosted-forest - Another new CA flag, `useExactAllocations` was introduced to allow to further reduce the memory footprint on GPU by computing the exact number of doublets before allocating their container. This leads to another potential memory saving but comes at the cost of one event synchronisation, whose impact on timing strongly depends on how much the GPU queue is full. The flag is disabled by default, since the trade-off is not currently worth it and memory reduction has been achieved in other key areas by cost-free developments - A lot of developments have gone into reducing the memory footprint of the entire CA chain. While most benefits are observed when using stubs, the default configuration also benefits from some improvements that specifically targeted the heaviest consumers of memory (doublets, triplets, tracks) - Some other miscellaneous improvements include `OneToManyAssoc` zeroing using a device memset and `bulkFill` gaining a content-capacity overflow guard **Note** This PR needs https://github.com/cms-data/RecoTracker-FinalTrackSelectors/pull/16 to be tested **Update 21/09** The material map is now served as a binary file via `cms-data`. See https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51915#issuecomment-5766520274 #### PR validation - Running `scram b runtests` locally shows no failures - `runTheMatrix.py -l limited -i all --ibeos` runs fine locally - Physics performance has been validated on a few samples (TTbar, high pT QCD and Z' M6000), showing PixelTracks efficiency on par with the current baseline, with much improved track parameters and resolutions and reduced fake rate: [Efficiency vs eta](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/PR1_prompt_ITACA/MTV/TTbar/overlay/hltGeneral_hltAssociatorByHits+hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/effic.png) | [Efficiency vs pT](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/PR1_prompt_ITACA/MTV/TTbar/overlay/hltGeneral_hltAssociatorByHits+hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/efficPt.png) :-------------------------:|:-------------------------: | [Fake rate vs eta](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/PR1_prompt_ITACA/MTV/TTbar/overlay/hltGeneral_hltAssociatorByHits+hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/fakerate.png) | [pT resolution](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/PR1_prompt_ITACA/MTV/TTbar/overlay/hltGeneral_hltAssociatorByHits+hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/ptres_vs_eta_Sigma.png) | All plots are available [here](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/PR1_prompt_ITACA/MTV/) **Note** A new workflow such as `37834.7512` can be used to test the new ITACA prompt iteration on TTBar 200 PU. The old "PixelTriplets" workflows (offsets .406-.408) have been replaced with the new ITACA prompt iteration equivalents (validation and profiling) as per https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51915#discussion_r4050021029 This PR also changes the default behaviour of the `ngtScouting` procModifier, replacing the extended PixelTracks with ITACA prompt iteration **Review note** A bunch of new files is related to the mechanism to retrain the new CA modules and HP selector, ~with 80% of added lines coming from the material map~. Tiny changes especially in tracks dxy, dz and chi2 are expected from the fix in 159acfa3
title: [NGT] Implement ITACA prompt iteration
